svg.title: The reinforcement-learning loop
svg.desc: A two-part cycle. The agent, a small neural network of a few thousand numbers, sends an action to the world: turn, thrust, or fire. The world is the orbitduel physics simulation, with gravity, thrust and lasers. It sends back two things on every step. The first is an observation, a short list of numbers describing the situation, eight of them for the survival task and nineteen for the duel. The second is a reward, a single number that is positive for winning and negative for falling into the hole. The reward is the only teacher in the system: nobody ever tells the agent which action was correct, so it must work that out from the number alone. Observation and reward arrive together in the same step, drawn separately here because they play different roles. One pass around this loop is one step, and training repeats it hundreds of thousands of times.
svg.text: One trip around the loop is one step. Training takes hundreds of thousands of them.
Nobody ever says which action was right. The reward is the only teacher.
